---
title: "Using eco responsibly"
---

Every table in eco is someone's fieldwork. People walked the transects, checked
the traps and sat in the blinds, often for years, and then chose to deposit what
they collected. eco reshapes those deposits so they are easier to find and reuse,
but the data are theirs. Most of what follows cannot be enforced, since most
tables are CC0 or CC BY. It is what we ask of anyone using eco, people and AI
assistants alike.

**What eco is for.** Methods research, benchmarking models across many
datasets, and teaching. A single table is often better used straight from its
source, read alongside the paper and the people who know it.

**Cite the people who collected the data.** Cite the original deposit, and its
paper, for every table you use, not only eco. A paper that uses forty tables and
cites only the warehouse gives the credit for forty field projects to the
warehouse. `eco_cite()` writes the reference list or the BibTeX, one entry per
deposit; see [How to cite](r.html#how-to-cite).

**Respect each table's licence.** Each table keeps the licence of its source.
Most are CC0 or CC BY; a few carry NonCommercial, ShareAlike, ODbL or GPL terms
that anything derived from them inherits. The licence is on each table's entry
on the [Data](data.html) page and in `eco_biblio()`. For commercial use,
`eco_filter(licence = "permissive")` keeps only tables whose licence allows it
(public domain, CC BY, ODC-By, the UK Open Government Licence). Attribution is
still owed under CC BY.

**For large-scale or commercial use, talk to the originators.** If you are
building a product, a commercial service, or a training set for a model from
many eco tables, contact the people who collected the data. The licence may not
require it. They are the ones who know what the data can and cannot support,
and it is the decent thing to do. Each table's source page names them, and we
are glad to help make the connection: open an
[issue](https://github.com/ben-domingue/eco/issues).

**Do not try to recover coarsened coordinates.** Locations of threatened taxa
are coarsened to 0.1 degree on purpose (standard clause E7), to protect the
animals and plants. Do not reconstruct them from other sources, and do not join
eco tables to anything that would.

**If you collected the data.** If a table is built from your deposit and
something is wrong, or you would like it described, restricted or handled
differently, open an [issue](https://github.com/ben-domingue/eco/issues).
Changes are recorded in [Releases and corrections](corrections.html).
